evidence.producer: PROVISIONAL: src/common/ owns deliberately small cross-layer identities and pure numeric helpers; include/minic/compiler.h owns public translation-unit entrypoint and diagnostic type. Those contracts are not a second owner of Frontend C semantics, Core verification or physical target ABI.
consumers: src/common/integer_bits.h:minic_integer_mask64/minic_integer_sign_extend64 define pure bit geometry, consumed by Frontend integer/const parsing, Compiler local facts/lowering, Core Module fragment verification and Target source-policy/global serialization; callers own signed overflow and C-type width policy.

src/common/calling_convention.h defines an execution identity enum DEFAULT vs MS_X64 shared by frontend/type.h, core/core_type.h and target/target_info.h. Source C prototype legality remains Frontend; actual register-bank placement remains x86 Target, not Common.

src/common/call_frame_address.h defines return/frame builtin category used by source builtin admission, Core semantics and target support gates, without introducing a Core dependency on a concrete AST.
src/common/machine_builtin_effect.h defines sealed read/write effect identities for target machine builtins; Core CALL effects do not carry architecture-specific C builtin spellings.

include/minic/compiler.h supplies the stable public minic_compile_preprocessed_file compatibility path, explicit-target for_target entrypoint, function-sections policy and diagnostic schema. src/compiler/compiler.c implements these as one actual compiler transaction and a default-target wrapper, not duplicate compiler backends.

src/frontend/type.h and src/core/core_type.h consume Common calling-convention identity but keep independently owned C source type descriptors versus immutable per-TU Core execution types. src/target/target_info.h uses the same small shared identity without adopting frontend source representation.
evidence.functional_path: C10 PROVISIONAL common contract graph: public compile API/Diagnostic -> driver and Compiler's one whole-TU transaction; shared enum identities in src/common give SourcePolicy, Frontend, Core and Target a stable cross-stage vocabulary, without assigning shared ownership of C syntax or physical ABI. Pure integer bit geometry flows into Frontend/Compiler/Core/Target, but target-specific storage widths, signedness, overflow traps and machine instructions remain at their owning layers. Legacy public wrappers remain semantically active for default target; do not delete as textual duplicates.
limitations: UNTRUSTED C10 proposal only. This is initial cross-layer identity sampling, not a complete dependency-graph, ABI compatibility or header audit.
A common enum or pure helper does NOT prove same physical ABI/ISA behavior; source C calling convention legality and machine register plan are deliberately distinct owners.
Stable numeric C type kinds and public default-target wrappers have existing ABI/serialized compatibility obligations; do not remove or renumber due to apparent obsolescence.
Potential duplicate arithmetic helpers require true producer/consumer policy comparison and negative tests before consolidating; no bug or dead-code claim was established.
Separately audit include/minic public API backwards compatibility, C11/C++ linkage, compile modes and header dependency boundaries.
